title: Nondeterministic host for masked selection
statement: Let $V$ be a language of binary strings in $\mathrm{P}$, and let $C,c\in\mathbb{N}$. There exist $K,e\in\mathbb{N}$ and a nondeterministic finite Turing machine $N$ such that, for every binary string $x$, there are a natural number $s$ and a Boolean mask $m$ with exactly $C(|x|+1)^c$ true entries and $s+|m|\le K(|x|^e+1)$. For every binary string $w$ of length $K(|x|^e+1)$, the computation of $N$ on $x$ using choices $w$ halts and outputs the single bit indicating whether $x$ followed by the subsequence selected by the true entries of $m$ among the first $|m|$ bits of $w$ belongs to $V$.
hypotheses_covered: $V$ is a language over the binary alphabet
